01 / CALIBER

Reachability caliber — indicative, pending field-audit calibration

GraphThe five roads.geojson centrelines, noded at their crossings; 20,141 m totalprovisional geometry · not a survey quantity
AccessEach node joins by its shortest straight stub; stub length counts against the budget
AI-onR_on = 300 m network distance (~4 min at 1.25 m/s, continuous multichannel handover)
AI-offR_off = 150 m network distance (one fixed multichannel totem plus the staffed help point)
BandReachable linework buffered to a service band of half-width w = 40 m (round caps; arcs approximated by inscribed polygons at 12 segments per quadrant — third-party recomputation must use the same resolution to match digit for digit)
Gapgap = domain(300 m) − domain(150 m): space reached only while AI is on

This drawing uses the full-network radius convention: both states sit on one complete network and measure the shrinkage of the guidance range; it stands beside the fixed-interface convention of the OP-04 chain replay (which judges whether an equivalent route exists), and figures must not be converted between the two. No value is stated for ai_off_service_equivalence_gap: metrics.json registers it status=unknown, pending paired task testing. The gap area is only that metric's geometric audit target — not a coverage commitment, a compliance conclusion or a service-level promise.

03 / AI ON = AI OFF

The spatial form of the equivalence claim

AI ONMultichannel wayfinding hands over along the network; the domain extends to 300 m.
=
AI OFFOnly the fixed totem and staffed help point remain; the domain shrinks to 150 m.

Equivalence is the service floor this proposal commits to; the coral gap marks where that commitment is not yet met — an audit target, not a claim of compliance today.
